incident: podman aardvark-dns EADDRNOTAVAIL from zombie containers with dead netns blocked the autonomous-QA matrix backend bring-up
classification: container-runtime infrastructure (not a host Class I/II/III per §6.M — host was continuously up 6d20h, no reboot, no suspend, no signout)
discovered_by: run-matrix.sh --backend goapi --subsets rutracker --queries 1080p keystone re-verification failing at ./start.sh compose up
symptom_verbatim: netavark: error while applying dns entries: aardvark-dns failed to start: Error from child process
Error starting server failed to bind udp listener on 10.89.0.1:53: IO error: Cannot assign requested address (os error 99)
failed to bind udp listener on 10.89.2.1:53: IO error: Cannot assign requested address (os error 99)

root_cause.confirmed: Six podman containers reported State.Status=running while their recorded PIDs were dead (no /proc/<pid>/ns/net) — zombie containers with torn-down network namespaces. aardvark-dns is a single shared daemon that, on any network change (e.g. bringing up a new container on lava_lava-net 10.89.3.0/24), re-binds the .1 gateway of EVERY DNS-enabled podman network. The gateways of two networks owned by zombie stacks — 10.89.0.1 (lava-thinker) and 10.89.2.1 (proxy-dynamic) — had no interface assigned because those bridges were gone, so aardvark's bind failed with EADDRNOTAVAIL, which blocked ALL new DNS-network container starts host-wide.
evidence: uptime: up 6 days 20:37, boot 2026-06-25 12:50 — NO reboot
per-container liveness probe: lava-api-go-thinker/lava-postgres-thinker/proxy-gluetun/proxy-redis/proxy-postgres/proxy-healthd = DEAD-pid; helixcode-caddy/proxy-admin = live-pid
podman network reload --all failed with 'netavark: setns: IO error: Invalid argument (os error 22)' — confirms the target netns are invalid (zombie)
network subnet map: lava-thinker=10.89.0.0/24 gw 10.89.0.1 (dns=true); proxy-dynamic=10.89.2.0/24 gw 10.89.2.1 (dns=true) — exactly the two failing binds

eliminated: host suspend/hibernate/signout (§6.M: no logind transitions implicated; not a Class I/II/III host event)
missing VPN egress (host routes through Mullvad wg0-mullvad, exit 141.98.253.210 mullvad_exit_ip=true — container egress to trackers is available without the gluetun container)

remediation.principle: destroy the DEAD + rebuild (operator standing container-hygiene mandate); scoped to not disturb genuinely-live other-project containers (helixcode-caddy, proxy-admin) or their data
actions: podman rm -f Lava-owned zombies: lava-api-go-thinker, lava-postgres-thinker, lava-api-go, lava-migrate, lava-postgres
podman network rm -f lava-thinker (clears 10.89.0.1 blocker) and lava_lava-net (recreated fresh by ./start.sh)
podman rm -f the confirmed-dead HelixProxy proxy-dynamic backends (proxy-gluetun/redis/postgres/healthd) — un-restartable dead netns; HelixProxy rebuilds from its own compose
remediation.verification: throwaway container on a fresh DNS-enabled network (podman network create lava-aardvark-test; podman run --rm --network lava-aardvark-test alpine echo AARDVARK_OK) printed AARDVARK_OK — aardvark-dns confirmed healed

secondary_finding.double-launch-125: A first (pre-network-fix) run-matrix process was in a start.sh retry loop and SUCCEEDED the moment aardvark healed (backend up, emulator booted, Challenge70 gradle running); a redundant second launch then failed with podman-compose exit status 125 on a container-name conflict. Lesson: do not relaunch run-matrix while a prior invocation may still be retrying. The harness itself is correct once the network is healthy.

anti_bluff_note: No test was reported green during this. The keystone was RE-RUN clean after remediation to obtain real end-to-end evidence rather than trusting the 2026-06-30 keystone result. Per §6.J/§6.L: infra being green is necessary, never sufficient — the QA verdict comes from the actual Challenge70 run against the real backend + real emulator.

falsifiability_rehearsal.note: This is an infrastructure-remediation incident, not a production-code defect, so the rehearsal is on the REMEDIATION's own claim ('aardvark-dns is healed') rather than a source-code mutation. The RED state was the pre-existing zombie condition; the GREEN state is the post-remediation probe. Both were physically observed (§6.N.1.3).
falsifiability_rehearsal.bluff_classification: infra-green-masking — a container runtime that reports containers 'Up' (podman DB) while their netns are dead, so 'the stack is up' is a bluff; the honest signal is whether a NEW container can actually start on a DNS-enabled network.
falsifiability_rehearsal.mutation: The naturally-occurring fault itself: 6 zombie containers (dead netns) left two DNS-enabled networks' gateways unbindable, so aardvark-dns could not start.
falsifiability_rehearsal.observed_failure_RED: Before remediation, `./start.sh` (api-go) compose-up FAILED: 'netavark: aardvark-dns failed to start: ... failed to bind udp listener on 10.89.0.1:53 / 10.89.2.1:53: Cannot assign requested address (os error 99)'. `podman network reload --all` FAILED with 'setns: Invalid argument (os error 22)'. No new DNS-network container could start.
falsifiability_rehearsal.observed_pass_GREEN: After removing the dead Lava zombies + the two drifted networks (lava-thinker, proxy-dynamic), the falsification probe `podman network create lava-aardvark-test && podman run --rm --network lava-aardvark-test alpine echo AARDVARK_OK` printed AARDVARK_OK — a fresh container provably starts on a DNS-enabled network. The subsequent full keystone (backend up + containerized-KVM emulator boot + Challenge70) then ran end-to-end, confirming the heal in the real gate path.
falsifiability_rehearsal.reverted: n/a — the dead zombies were the fault; removing them is the fix, not a test mutation to revert. The GREEN probe is repeatable.
